b: We've been together for 13 years, married for 3. When I met him we were in uni, young and most of the time drunk! He was the life and soul of the party, the class clown, the one that everyone liked because he could just talk to anybody and make anyone laugh. I was introverted and nervous to be away from home and his confidence was extremely attractive to me. This lasted a few years, he had a good group of friends in uni, was social, went out with them and although his outgoingness seemed slightly less than when we first met, he was still a confident guy.

We were (and are still) obsessed with one another, we're soul mates and love spending as much time together as we can however as the years have gone on, I've realised that he's actually cut out just about everyone other than me. We are in a bubble just us. And although I'm not the most social person, I continue to meet up with friends, go out with my work collegues and have a good relationship with my family. He however, hasn't got that anymore through choice. In his mind everyone's annoying, frustrating, he can't be bothered meeting people, forgets to reply to family and just doesn't want to step out of his comfort zone. Even at work, where he's been for 2 years, he hates everyone. Every day he comes back he complains about his colleagues and how annoying they are and I'm not saying he's making it up but I just think how can every single person be annoying? How can he not connect with anyone anymore?

I would say he meets with a friend maybe twice a year and even then he complains he can't be bothered and says things like 'I hate everyone except you'. I used to love the it's us against the world feeling but now I've realised it's not sustainable.

I would never split with him, as I say he's my soul mate, but it's so much pressure to be his everything. For example, if we have an argument (which all couples do of course) he'll say 'I don't have anyone to talk to but you' which feels a bit like emotional blackmail. I need to be able to voice issues without feeling like he's lost the only person on his side. He needs to have other people he can talk to about things. His mum has made comments about how he is distant and she wishes he spoke to her and his dad more and he bats this off saying 'they could reach out to me'.

He sometimes says that he's not got any friends which upsets me but I think he doesn't seem to want them. There are people that try to connect with him and meet up but he never wants to. I'm not sure what I should do here, I feel like I'm walking on eggshells but this is a very similar situation to my parents relationship, my dad has no friends and makes my mum feel guilty for going out with hers, and I can't bare to think that that's our future. I want the old version of him back, I need to see him outside of our bubble, interacting with other people, being confident, socialising.
How do I approach this without upsetting him?
